page: Microsoft Azure M192lds_v4 is a high-capacity memory-optimized virtual machine delivered on the Microsoft Hyper-V platform. Built on the x86_64 architecture with dedicated Intel processors, the instance delivers 192 dedicated vCPUs paired with 3072.0 GB of system memory. This architecture yields a dense memory ratio of 16.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, designed to maintain large working sets entirely in memory without relying on constant external storage retrieval.

Storage capability includes 7087 GB of direct-attached local NVMe SSD capacity alongside compatibility with Azure Premium Storage. The high-speed local disk configuration allows systems to handle rapid swap, tempdb, caching, and scratch operations directly on host-attached solid-state media. The instance operates without hardware GPU acceleration and does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring standard cloud networking constructs for external connectivity.

The primary architectural tradeoff of the M192lds_v4 lies in its dedicated scale; consolidating 192 cores and three terabytes of RAM onto a single instance simplifies architecture by avoiding distributed cluster overhead, but it requires workloads capable of scaling across high core counts. The instance is structured for large in-memory transactional databases such as SAP HANA, massive relational databases, large-scale data warehousing, real-time analytics engines, and enterprise resource planning systems.
description: Microsoft Azure M192lds_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine configured for large enterprise workloads. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance supplies 192 dedicated vCPUs built on an x86_64 Intel processor architecture. It is equipped with 3072 GB of total system memory, providing a high memory allocation of 16.0 GB per vCPU. Storage architecture combines Premium Storage capability with a bundled 7087 GB local NVMe SSD, providing substantial high-speed temporary storage alongside compute resources. The instance operates without discrete GPU accelerators and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. With its massive memory pool and high core count, this server profile balances extensive memory density against compute resources without requiring multi-node clustering. The hardware profile is engineered primarily for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, including large in-memory databases, large-scale enterprise resource planning systems, extensive analytics platforms, and intensive data processing pipelines that require direct access to multi-terabyte working memory and fast local scratch space.
